data.objectivesText: Collect 10 Pilfered Windstones from the Highlands Bandits in the Shen'dar Highlands.
description: We are relying on windstones more and more for day to day living here on Zephras so we try and maintain a cache of them in reserve for emergencies. Lately I've noticed some go missing from our stores.
We've found windstones on bandits we've captured recently, and I suspect they are behind our shortages.
If you find yourself near the bandit cave to the north, mind knocking a few heads together and reclaiming some of our pilfered windstones for me?
data.partialDialogue: These sneakthieves have likely been breaking into our supplies for months. I tried to convince Aonda to put a raid together to clear out that bandit cave for good, but she didn't want to pull the few peacekeepers we have away from the village.With the cultists at Falaath Village to the south growing in numbers, I suppose I can't fault her for that.
data.turnInDialogue: Thanks ‹class›. This should help us get by for now. If we can't get the supply routes squared away soon though, a few stolen windstones will be the least of our worries.

data.objectivesText: Report to Yorana Windyreed at the eastern watchtower in the Gustberry Lowlands.
description: I've just received word that the cult is attacking the pylon watchtower just outside of town! I've sent the few extra peacekeepers we have here to try and break through the enemy back line to relieve the defenders, but any additional help could mean the difference between our people there living or dying.
Please leave immediately for the east watchtower and provide whatever aid you can.
My lieutenant Yorana Windyreed led the relief force. If she still lives she can tell you how best to help.
data.turnInDialogue: We are holding them off for now, but they have greater numbers and our fighters are starting to get tired. We need to do something to break the stalemate, and do it fast.

Many among us are afraid.

I come with an offer. Fight the cultists for us, and bring us the ears of those you kill. We will reward you for each that you return with in both coin and, in time, access to our secrets should you prove yourself to be a true friend.

description: You've got that "High Order" look to you. Those with Highborne ancestry always seem to have a slight twinkle in their eyes that gives it away. Before I properly put you to work around here, you should check in with our resident High Order elder Rathiril Sunlance. You can find him here in the main lodge, just around the corner from me.
Oh, and check in with Coriella Calmbreeze as well, she runs the local inn and can provide lodging and supplies, should you need them.
data.turnInDialogue: Checked in with Rathiril then? Great. Lots of tension between the High Order and the Windshapers these days, but they keep things civil here in Shen'dar. Well, at least in the village anyway. What happens out in the wilds stays in the wilds.Now that that's done, you look like someone who might be looking for something to do with their hands. I've got a few things that need doing, if you are game for a bit of work?

data.objectivesText: Collect 15 Windstone Clusters from Raw Windstones in Thendal Grove.
description: Windstones are a critical resource on Zephras Isle as they contain the raw, concentrated energy of the winds themselves. The wind elementals who used to live here on zephras with us vanished several centuries ago, and since then, the magic that sustains this island is slowly fading. Not without limitations, the Windstones are still a reliable energy source, and are incredibly valuable to us.
You'll find raw Windstones scattered around the grove, think you can help me harvest them?
data.partialDialogue: Hello there, ‹class›.
data.turnInDialogue: Thank you very much for these. As elves we all have a deep connection to magic and these windstones are becoming more and more precious as the magic imbued into this island by the great anchor pylons continues to fade.windstones aren't the only beneficial thing you can harvest from the land. Please, take one of these manuals.

data.objectivesText: Find Riaani Nightwind on the west side of Valanaar.
description: Historically, the Windshapers have seen to the tending of the magical instruments and devices that were gifted to us by the spirits of the wind. This includes the myriad of magical constructs around the island. Since the spirits left us, only a scant few of these are still functional.

One of the few remaining working constructs in Valanaar has become damaged. One of our artisans was dispatched to help, but he may be in need of aid. Travel to the west end of the city and offer any assistance you can.
data.turnInDialogue: <Riaani's face is buried under the heaving armor plates of the construct, attempting to work on the mechanisms underneath. He does not notice your presence at all.>Storms curse where is the core?! Who thought it would be a good idea to remove the Gyrozephyr as well? It's a miracle this construct's winds haven't dissipated entirely by now!

data.objectivesText: Gather 10 Wind Hollow Essences from Wind Hollows in the Shadowgale Forest.
description: The paramount concern of the Windshapers is to better understand why the spirits left us, and what we may be able to do to bring them back. One curious fixture of Shadowgale Forest to the north is the presence of a curious form of wind sprite that some call "hollows". We know little of them and why they are there, but we do know that they first started to appear after the spirits of the wind left us.
I need you to go there and disperse them. Gather the remains and bring them back here.
data.partialDialogue: Shadowgale Forest is a dangerous place. Some even say its haunted. I'm quite sure that I don't believe that, but I do know that its not for the faint hearted, or the unprepared.
data.turnInDialogue: Handling these essences fills me with a sense of... deep disquiet. I can almost feel a malevolent, regretful aura emanating from them. It's enough to make me faint.<Endaria shudders slightly.>I do not look forward to studying these further.

description: Oh, hello. Ayessa sent you to assist me? Very well then.
Not sure what an obvious novice like yourself can do, but if you give me a moment to pull my head out of this construct's innards I might have a few ideas of things you can do to help.
data.partialDialogue: I can't imagine why anyone would want to steal these components from this construct. Other than the gyrozephyr these components have almost no practical application. Even the gyro would be nigh-useless outside of its intended purpose.
data.turnInDialogue: Thank you for scavenging these materials. I imagine that some of this wasn't terribly easy to get.With these parts I can get the construct up and running again. From there we can just hope that its memory is intact and it can tell us who took its components.

data.objectivesText: Report back to Ayessa Dawnsinger in Valanaar.
description: Brightwish, eh? So the High Order wanted to remove these components for some reason. But why though?

The High Order has always been meddlesome, constantly wanting to experiment with the wind spirits' magic. They are too bold by a mile, and we've strictly forbade them from meddling with knowledge under Windshaper purview, but lately they've been testing our patience.
I think you should report what you've learned back to Ayessa Dawnsinger. She can instruct you further on what to do.
data.turnInDialogue: Very interesting, so it was the High Order that was responsible for the construct breaking down?I know Belathaan. He's Valennia Stormfist's cousin and his mother was actually a Windshaper. It's disappointing that he was involved in this.I need to reflect on this for a moment.

data.objectivesText: Collect 10 Al'Aketh Windstone Charms from the corpses of Al'Aketh cultists in the Gustberry Lowlands.
description: A number of our Windshaper novices were found dead in the Highlands this morning. We can't be certain but there is a strong chance that the Al'Aketh are responsible. Windshapers trade blood for blood, every time.
Head north and kill any Al'Aketh you encounter. Bring me their windstone prayer charms as proof of the deed. We do not forgive and we do not forget.
data.partialDialogue: The Al'Aketh have engaged in their bloody zealotry for far too long. This is only the start of the reckoning they face.
data.turnInDialogue: <Ayessa looks shaken and distant as you hand her the windstone charms.>Don't mind me, Sladkiy. Today has merely been... a trying day. Thank you for your service to the windshapers thus far.

data.objectivesText: Confront Belthaan Brightwish along the road to the Shrine of Akir.
description: The High Order has been warned of the consequences of meddling with the Windshaper's affairs. I think we need to make an example out of Belathaan and send him back to the High Order with a few bruises and a healthy respect for the boundaries we set.

Belathaan was seen leaving town, traveling north towards the Shrine of Akir. I don't know why he was going there, but confronting him alone on the road is the safest option. Find him, and put a bit of fear into his heart.
data.turnInDialogue: Wait--what?! Belathaan... is dead?<Ayessa listens as you give your account of what occurred.>The High Order was meeting with the Al'Aketh to discuss peace? There is no peace with the cult, they are murderous zealots. What was Elaadrin thinking sending Belathaan to treat with them alone?Pay this no mind, Marabi. You are not at fault for this. The arrogance of the High Order is to blame, yet again. You were merely in the right place at the wrong time.

Seek out Belann Windwood in Valanaar. He has been crafting staves and wands for the High Order for over a century, so you will be in good hands.
data.turnInDialogue: Ah, you must be Laderoth? It is heartening to see young mages eager to learn our ways and history. Come, I will explain the next steps to crafting your spell focus.

data.objectivesText: Bring a Wind-Infused Bough to Belann Windwood in Valanaar.
description: It is a time-honored tradition for young mages to create their own spell focus when they have shown a certain degree of magical proficiency. This is typically done by gathering a fallen branch from our oldest trees, as they have some lingering traces of elemental wind.

I have found the most ideal ones to be near the wind shrine, just south of Falaath Village. Go and bring me back a large branch and I will teach you about the traditions as we create your spell focus.
data.partialDialogue: Every year that passes in Zephras sees fewer and fewer of those who are gifted with a talent for magic.I am glad to see young mages such as yourself participate in our oldest traditions to help keep our history and culture alive and well.
data.turnInDialogue: Thank you, Amidaru. I can indeed feel the elemental energies in this bough waiting to be harnessed by those that have the gift to do so. This will make an excellent spell focus.Did this branch sing to you, perhaps? It has often been the case that the branch picks the ‹class›, and not the other way around.

description: Lorthuna fled up to the spires above using some sort of portal. Ayessa and Elaadrin went in after her. That was just a few moments ago.
I'm afraid I took one too many hits and this is where I stay. Go through the portal, find Elaadrin and help them stop Lorthuna.
Unless that help that Elaadrin and Ayessa said they sent for arrives soon, you are on your own from here. Good luck, ‹class›.
data.turnInDialogue: I sent a few of our remaining mages to ensure that Valennia and her forces were able to escape as well. She should be resting at High Elder Shadowsong's residence now.Ansirem had to return to Azeroth, but he and I discussed the next steps for the High Order before he departed. We survived the day, but Zephras is dangerously vulnerable now and we must make plans for what is to come.

data.objectivesText: Speak with Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar.
description: Muln has told me much of the elemental lords and I am afraid that we have good reason to fear Al'Akir. Now that the wards that have hidden Zephras from his view are down, we are utterly defenseless.. If he chooses to attack us, we stand no chance against him here in his own domain.
High Elder Shadowsong needs to know of the danger we are in, and more importantly, what our intentions are for our mission to Azeroth. We will find the means to save our home. I swear it.
data.turnInDialogue: <Talaanis Shadowsong listens intently as you tell him of what transpired above the Shrine of Akir, and of Ayessa's plan to leave Zephras Isle.>I need to reflect on this further, but looking at the upside, we have rid ourselves of Lorthuna and deprived the cult of their leader. Our home has not been invaded yet and on the timeline of elemental gods, it could be years... decades even, before Al'Akir deigns to turn his attention to us.There is much to fear now, but much to celebrate as well.

description: Whatever reason the cult has for attacking the tower, it's not worth losing our people over.

I'd like for you to head to the southwest and check in on that watchtower for us. Find the peacekeepers there and tell them to head back to the village. Holding that tower is not worth the lives it would cost and I'd rather concentrate the defenders we do have here to protect our citizens.
Peacekeeper Vaaniel is in charge, let him know to head back here as quickly as possible. Hurry!
data.turnInDialogue: <The body here is somewhat fresh, clearly only recently having been killed. Judging by the burns and scorch marks on this peacekeeper's skin, its clear that they were killed by the cult's storm-wielding spellcasters.>

description: Since you are going to Valanaar anyway, please deliver the signet ring you recovered from the tower to Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar.

He will want this back, and more importantly, he will want to learn the fate of his nephew. Talaanis is the High Elder of Zephras Isle and more importantly, he is a good man who is well loved by the people, despite our current hardships. It pains me to think of how he will react to this news. Please express my condolences for his loss.
data.partialDialogue: What is that you have for me? Oh... oh no.
data.turnInDialogue: I... am very sorry to hear that my nephew is dead. I thank you kindly for recovering this, and bringing it to me.It's not common that such capable young shen'dorei come down from the highlands. If you need work, please speak with Valennia Stormfist, the captain of the peacekeepers here in Valanaar. These days we need all the help we can get.

data.objectivesText: Kill Skyhoppers in Valanaar until you've eliminated 8 enchanted Skyhoppers.
description: We've been bugged.

It's skyhopper season in the lowlands, which means the pests are everywhere. One of the High Order mages reported that one of the insects that they killed had an enchantment of some kind placed upon it. When we inspected it closely it seems to be some sort of listening spell.

We suspect that the cult is using these enchanted insects as spies. Go and exterminate them for us. You won't be able to tell which are enchanted by looking at them, so you'll just have to kill them all.
data.turnInDialogue: I'm sure there are more of these critters around Valanaar, but every enchanted skyhopper we stomp out makes the city just a tiny bit safer.

Many skyborne love to adorn their hair with vibrant plumes and the down feathers of a hippogryph are exceptionally vibrant and more importantly, silky soft.
If you are heading that way, try and gather as many of the fallen feathers as you can from in and around their nesting grounds. Do be careful, as wild hippogryph are not tolerant of guests.
data.partialDialogue: What beautiful things did you bring me?
data.turnInDialogue: It might seem a bit of a vain triviality, gathering feathers for our hair. However, even in times like these, one needs to embrace the small joys as much as possible.If one thing I create brings someone joy, then I will consider that to be a good day. Thank you for bringing me these and helping me bring some joy to Zephras.

data.lede: A level 13 quest for the Alliance, from level 7.

data.objectivesText: Speak with Randal Emerson in Stormwind Keep to receive further instructions. Use the instructions received to locate and speak with King Magni Bronzebeard, High Tinker Mekkatorque, and Tyrande Whisperwind.
description: Stormwind, Ironforge, and Darnassus all have unique peoples and cultures. As a guest of the Alliance here on Azeroth, you should take some time to visit each of our capital cities in turn.
Speak with Randal Emerson in the southern antechamber for directions to get you started.
data.turnInDialogue: Ah, you are back.I hope your adventures have given you a sense of the scale and wonder of our world. I know it must seem overwhelming to you, but if you are to help your people, you must be prepared for whatever may come your way while you are on Azeroth.While you wait for your order to establish itself in Dalaran, I suggest you turn your attention to the lands around Stormwind. Westfall in particular can always use more strong adventurers to lend them aid, if you are willing.

data.name: The Skybreaker Bulwark
data.lede: A level 10 quest for both factions, from level 10.

knownStatus.raw: New in Forever.  From Wowhead’s Forever database.
knownStatus.changeNote: New in Forever.  From Wowhead’s Forever database.

data.objectivesText: Reclaim the Skybreaker Bulwark from Zaal Stormshield at the Shrine of Akir.
description: I am all that remains of the line of Skybreakers here on Zephras Isle. The rest were murdered by the Al'Aketh.

The only thing that outweighs my sorrow is my shame. My family's ancestral shield--the Skybreaker Bulwark--is now in the hands of a cultist named Zaal Stormshield. Family lore holds no harm may befall a worthy wielder of this shield.
Zaal is not worthy, of that I am sure. Find this man at the Shrine of Akir and reclaim my shield from him. Do this and I will teach you the Skybreaker Defense.
data.partialDialogue: <Seena nods curtly at you.>
data.turnInDialogue: You have done what I could not and restored my family honor. For this, I will bestow a gift that few on Zephras are worthy to receive. I will teach out the secrets of the Skybreaker Defense.Also, you will need a shield to put what I have to teach you into practice. Please, take this one. I have little use for it now that the Skybreaker Bulwark has been returned to me.Banu'Adoraah, friend.

data.objectivesText: Speak with Urs'endris near the falls northeast of Valanaar.
description: Greetings, ‹name›. You have progressed in your druidic studies far enough that I think it is time for you to meet one of the great spirits that reside here on Zephras. Urs'endris is a wise and noble spirit, who has taught druids how to take on the ursera shape for generations. Unfortunately his domain has begun to wither and fall into the sky like many other areas of Zephras.
To find him, travel northeast near the waterfall in the shadow of the Shrine of Akir. He should be able to instruct you further.
data.turnInDialogue: So, you wish to embrace the way of the claw, child? Very well. Let us speak.

data.objectivesText: Use the Taming Rod to tame a Vuldren Alpha in the Gustberry Lowlands. Practice your skills, then return the Taming Rod to Quel'ana Quickgale in Valanaar.
description: You've returned triumphant from taming two beasts, it's time now for your last trial. The winds of Zephras whisper of greater challenges ahead.
Take this Taming Rod and journey to the Gustberry Lowlands. There, tame a Vuldren Alpha and prove your mastery.
Complete this lesson and you'll be ready to learn the deeper ways of the hunter.
data.partialDialogue: You will learn, Naanariel, and one day you will be a great ‹class›.
data.turnInDialogue: Excellent, Naanariel! You are quite a fast learner. Now that you know the basics, I can teach you how to forge a lasting bond with an animal companion.Go with this knowledge and thrive. Be the ‹class› that Zephras Isle needs you to be.

description: You now have the power to tame a pet, but you must also gain the skills to train it. For this, there is none better than my sister, Quel'dora. She will give you the ability to train your new pet.
Go with the winds, young ‹class›.
data.turnInDialogue: A fledgling ‹class›, I see. Yes, I can bestow you with the skills you need to train and guide your pet. Not only will you be able to teach your pet new abilities, you will now be able to feed your pet, as well as revive it, should it fall in battle.Remember, Gei, always respect the balance and live in awe of nature around you. Now, go forth. We shall speak again, at a later date.

data.objectivesText: Speak with Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar.
description: Ansirem has told me much of the elemental lords and I am afraid that we have good reason to fear Al'Akir now that the wards that have hidden Zephras are down. If the Windlord chooses to attack us, we stand no chance to defend ourselves while we are here in his domain.
High Elder Shadowsong needs to know of the danger we are in, and more importantly, what our intentions are for our mission to Azeroth. We will find the means to save our home. I swear it.
data.turnInDialogue: <Talaanis Shadowsong listens intently as you tell him of what transpired above the Shrine of Akir, and of Elaadrin's plan to leave Zephras Isle.>I need to reflect on this further, but looking at the upside, we have rid ourselves of Lorthuna and deprived the cult of their leader. Our home has not been invaded yet, and on the timeline of elemental demigods, it could be years... decades even, before Al'Akir deigns to turn his attention to us.There is much to fear now, but much to celebrate as well.

data.objectivesText: Bring 2 Frostmane Bear Pendants to Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar.
description: Aye, the time's come, young shaman. Ye've grown stout and sturdy, like the stone beneath our boots. Takin' up the shaman's path shows ye've got the wisdom o' the mountain, even before ye've proven yerself.. Ye've the grit of stone to walk the earth's path.
But to earn its favor, ye must face it proper. South o' here, the Frostmane trolls live in a cave.
Bring me two of their necklaces they wear--crafted from the Iceclaw bears. Then we'll speak more of yer future.
data.partialDialogue: Patience, lad, is the earth's finest virtue. It's seen mountains crumble and rivers carve valleys - slow and stubborn, like a true ‹race›. The earth calls to ye now, for trouble brews on the horizon. Return successful, and ye'll be one step closer to bein' whole.Others may envy yer wisdom, but that's their burden to bear.
data.turnInDialogue: Well done, lad. Ye've proven yerself ready. Earth's the bedrock of all things. Strength, stamina, patience. It'll shield ye, but only if ye show it proper respect. Even stone can shift if slighted. Learn its ways, and ye'll grow wiser than most. Never forget the secrets it shares.I'll craft ye a sapta now - accept it, and ye'll walk the true path.

data.objectivesText: Find the Spirit Stone and drink the Earth Sapta.
description: Aye, sapta's a brew forged with magic, bindin' our spirit to the elements. Only a few shaman know the recipe, and it's nae for the weak-willed. Drink it, and ye will see what others can't. Hold true--it's only to be drunk in a sacred place.
Head north to the Spirit Stone, tucked at the end of a hidden path up the mountain. Drink it there... see what the earth has to show ye.
data.turnInDialogue: Ah... Thordin... the earth welcomes you, even in this frozen land. Bound in body and spirit, you'll walk forward knowing the mountains are your strength, the plains your patience, and the world your essence.To pass this rite, stand humbly before the earth. The other elements are not so still - they clash and roar. Learn their dual nature, even here among the snow and stone.

data.objectivesText: Bring the Rough Quartz to Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar.
description: Take this rough quartz from me and bring it to Teo Hammerstorm as proof o' our meeting. He will craft a totem for ye, and this pebble will be the heart o' it. As small as it may seem, ye will come to find that size does not matter, and that even the smallest o' things can outlast many others.
Be patient, ‹name›. Remain strong. And seek wisdom. This is what earth asks o' ye. In the end, ye shall become one with the earth--respect it as it shall respect ye.
data.partialDialogue: Ahh, ye've returned. If ye have the stone, it means the mountain's chosen ye true. I'll give ye the totem it promised. But if ye've come empty-handed, off with ye! The path ain't for those who forget their way.
data.turnInDialogue: Well done! Know this - totems ain't just a mark of yer place among shamans. They're tools, a focus for spells tied to stone, soil, and other elements. As ye grow wiser, more o' the mountain's power will open to ye. The trainers will know when yer ready for more. But for now, take this totem, and let the ground speak through ye.

data.objectivesText: Slay 6 High Order Apprentices in Shen'dar Highlands.
description: Be warned, members of the High Order have been seen in the vicinity of the standing stones north of the village. We have warned them time and again to not meddle at our sacred sites, but they are growing more bold in pushing us. Prove your resolve to us by going to the standing stones and dispersing them.
I am loathe to condone outright bloodshed, but do what you must to drive them off. Return to me when its done.
data.turnInDialogue: Direct conflict with our shen'dorei brothers and sisters only weakens us as a people, but decisive action must at times be taken to prevent greater tragedy.The mages of the High Order have zero regard for the consequences of their magical meddling. The forces that bind our island are fragile and vulnerable and all it could take is one thoughtless action to destroy our home.

data.objectivesText: Slay 6 Windshaper Novice Seers in Shen'dar Highlands.
description: The recent emergence of the ley lines on the surface of Zephras has been profound for our order. We have more direct and tangible access to the energies that permeate this place and it has increased our understanding of said magic greatly.
The Windshapers, however, view these emergences as scars on the land that must be "healed". This is an affront to our order and is something we simply cannot abide.
Go to the ley line in the forest to the southwest and drive off the Windshapers you find there.
data.turnInDialogue: Sometimes I find it hard to distinguish between the blind zealotry of the Al'Aketh cult, and the stubborn refusal of the Windshapers to change.If they truly believed the winds would guide us, they should be sensing the direction the winds are blowing and flow with them rather than against them.

data.objectivesText: Speak with Halaan Hawk-Eye and borrow his gift to view the anchor pylon in the distance.
description: Greetings, young ‹name›. I often times come here to look upon the ancient anchor pylon. Gifts from the spirits of the winds, they bind and sustain our island. Of late however, their magic has grown unstable and inconsistent.
They suffer no distress I can see. Their splendor has not changed.
If you'd like, I can lend you my gift to look upon them yourself.
data.partialDialogue: My gift is simple, and mundane. I cannot peer between worlds such as those with the skysight, nor can I draw upon the magic of the ley lines beneath Zephras like others can. But a gift it remains and I am grateful to have it.Appreciation of what you have is the key to happiness. Yearning for what you may have, or what you have lost, only leads to despair.
data.turnInDialogue: Thank you for taking a moment to share this with me. I will continue to watch over the grove, and ponder on the state of our homeland.

data.objectivesText: Speak to Tanis Alderwood in the Undercity.
description: A key tenant of being a paladin is the pursuit of divinity. This is not the pursuit of godhood, but merely the pursuit of good itself, for good's sake. We've all arrived at this place due to tragedy of one form or another, and it would be easy to lose that grace that defined us as paladins in life.
Go to the Undercity and seek out Tanis Alderwood in the Trade Quarter. They are in need, and they could benefit greatly from some grace.
data.turnInDialogue: You... you are a ‹class›? Please, do not hurt me. I-I know I'm not supposed to be panhandling. I have no quarrel with you or your order. Leave me be, I beg you!

description: Wait, you want to... help? Why would a paladin want to help a beggar like me?
Well, I suppose that you could be of some assistance.

Its my wife you see. She, well... she's falling apart. I mean that literally. The apothecaries can stitch her back together right as rain, but they are about the Dark Lady's business and none are available to help. If you could perhaps bring me some fresh cloth then I could at least make her a wrapping to hold her together while we wait for the apothecaries.
data.partialDialogue: I hope that this is no imposition upon you, goodly ‹class›.
data.turnInDialogue: This is very kind of you, ‹class›. Very kind indeed.

description: It's time to demonstrate your ability to channel one of the light's greatest gifts.

The item I just gave you is called the Symbol of Life. Take care, as it may cause you some discomfort to handle a talisman of the light such as this. The light may be anathema to the force that created us, but it is still our guide and ally. The pain reminds us of this.
Go see Deathguard Billmuth downstairs. He just arrived and he has petitioned us for aid. Show him and the Forsaken what a true paladin can do.
data.turnInDialogue: So you'll help me, then? Good, good. I'll admit I'm not proud of resorting to... well, resorting to asking paladins for aid. The priests waved me away and you might be my friend's only chance.Please, help me.

data.objectivesText: Take the Symbol of Life and use it to resurrect Deathguard Falgan at Venomweb Vale.
description: Falgan and I were sent on a mission to scout out scarlet activity in Venomweb Vale. We managed to sneak close enough to one of their camps to hear about new orders involving an attack on Brill. Before we could decide what to do next, I stepped on a twig and the noise alerted them to us.
Falgan yelled at me to run, so I ran. By the time I realized he wasn't with me, I was halfway to Brill. That brave idiot probably stayed behind to hold them off for me.
Please, find my friend and help him if you can.
data.turnInDialogue: I'm... back? And saved by a ‹class› no less? I see you carry a Symbol of Life. I've not seen one of those since... well, since before the war when Lordaeron was a very different place. I can only assume you are here to help. Billmuth and I were sent here to scout out the scarlet activity here, and we found out that they are planning some kind of attack.If you would be willing to help more, there may yet be more than you can do to help the Forsaken.

data.objectivesText: Find Bruegs Kindleborn in Dun Morogh.
description: It's been long since ye were last tested, ‹name›. Ye've shown patience, aye -- but now it's time ye learned of chaos... of destruction. Fire's call is loud, and if ye're ready to pay its price, it'll speak to ye.
Seek out Bruegs Kindleborn, far east in the mountains. He dwells in a cave above South Gate Outpost. He'll know if ye're truly ready.
data.turnInDialogue: Hmm... that elder sent ye, eh? Well, a ‹class›'s word is solid, so I'll not argue. That means ye're ready for the next sapta. The sapta of fire. I see it in yer eyes already -- the burnin', the hunger. Ye've tasted power, and now ye want more. But mind yerself, Shamfor. Remember what the stone taught ye. Fire's easy to wield, but harder to master. Know when to hold back.

data.objectivesText: Bring the Torch of the Dormant Flame to Braldir Ashmantle in Loch Modan.
description: Aye, ye've the strength to bear the totem o' fire, lad--but strength alone won't make ye ready.
Beyond the Valley o' Kings, in the crags of Loch Modan, lies a hidden path to one o' our sacred peaks. There, Braldir Ashmantle guards the Shrine o' the Dormant Flame.
Take this torch to him--it shows yer intent. Return it burnin' by the shrine's brazier, and I'll see ye earn the totem proper.
data.partialDialogue: Greetin's, Rhett. Ye've made it to the Shrine o' the Dormant Flame, eh? Not many do. Only those well-versed in the ‹class›'s path can grasp the secrets this place holds.Shame ye came all this way just to be turned back--the climb's no stroll through Dun Morogh. But I'm the shrine's keeper, and I won't be lettin' just any foot trod about.
data.turnInDialogue: Ah, me apologies, Rhett. Didn't spot the Torch in yer hand. An honor to meet ye proper.Many a wanderer climbs these heights chasin' tales of treasure or beasts, only to find naught but stone and silence. But we know better, don't we, Rhett?This shrine holds truths far deeper than the Alliance can fathom. To us, it's a sacred flame that waits to be awakened.

data.objectivesText: Bring 1 Fire Tar and 1 Reagent Pouch to Braldir Ashmantle in Loch Modan.
description: Bah, ye didn't trek all this way for tales, did ye, ‹name›? Ye seek the Eternal Flame and the fire totem.
First, ye'll need a sapta to bind yer spirit to the flame.

I'll craft it--but I'll need two things: fire tar from Tunnel Rat Geomancers in the kobold caves up north, and a reagent pouch from a Stonesplinter Seer lurkin' in the southern hills. Dangerous work, but worthy of the flame.
data.partialDialogue: Aye, I've near all I need for the fire sapta, Ukko--just missin' the fire tar and the seer's pouch. The tar's carried by Tunnel Rat Geomancers in the kobold caves up north. The pouch ye'll need to wrest from a Stonesplinter seer in the southern hills. These ingredients are bound to flame, as all true saptas must be. Their elemental ties make our craft strong.
data.turnInDialogue: These'll do fine, Ukko.Fire ain't just fury and ruin--mark me words. It's life, it's forge, it's the breath o' creation. All things are bound in balance. One force tempers the other, gives it meaning. Without shadow, light's but a glare. Without flame, stone's but cold memory.Masterin' magic means knowin' when to blend, not just burn. That's true wisdom, lad.

data.objectivesText: Defeat the Minor Manifestation of Fire, and place the Glowing Ember in the brazier atop the Shrine of Eternal Flame.
description: The fire sapta's ready, ‹name›. Now ye face the flame. Use it at the shrine, then climb to the peak. There, ye'll see the spirit--he'll not strike 'til ye do, but he'll know ye see him.
Strike fast, lad. The longer ye wait, the stronger he burns. When he falls, take his glowing embers and place 'em in the brazier. Light the torch and earn the fire's favor.
data.partialDialogue: The brazier stands about a third your height, with charred inscriptions along its smooth metal rails. The metal shows no signs of wear from the weather, and the bowl seated at the top of it feels cool to the touch.Blackrock mountain looms in the distance, in clear view to honor from this sacred place.
data.turnInDialogue: A white hot flame ignites within the bowl as you place the ember within. You can feel the magical effects of the sapta coursing through your body and the fire dances rhythmically before you.You place the top of the torch within the basin, and it immediately catches on fire. The smoke seems to drift towards the mountain of blackrock.

description: Torch firmly in hand, you turn away from the brazier and look out over Loch Modan. You feel an excitement tugging at your spirit as the wind picks up and forces the flame to dance violently.
You start off down the path back to Dun Morogh in search of Bruegs Kindleborn.
data.partialDialogue: Aye, Rhett? What do ye have there?
data.turnInDialogue: By Madoran's beard, yer spirit burns brighter than any torch I've laid eyes on, Rhett--and that's somethin' to be proud of.Keep walkin' this path, and the elements'll bend to yer will. Our kin will come to ye for wisdom and guidance. So let me be the first to offer me hearty congratulations -- and present ye with yer newest totem. Ye've earned it, flameborn.

data.objectivesText: Find and speak with Elegael Thornpaw in the northeastern part of Shadowgale Forest.
description: A moment, if you will ‹name›. Are you headed towards Shadowgale Forest? There is a druid conclave there in a cave to the northeast. I have been waiting on word from them but their correspondence is long overdue.
With Ban'aethall in ruins and all the unrest lately I worry something dire may have happened. Please, if you are able go, seek out Elegael Thornpaw and put my mind at ease.
data.turnInDialogue: Thank goodness our message got to Lotheluum. Wait, where are the rest of the reinforcements? Surely it is not just you they sent?<Elegael pales as you relay your conversation with Lotheluum.>So the message did not get through. We are in dire straights indeed then.It seems we must handle this on our own. Time is of the essence.

knownStatus.changeNote: New in Forever.  From Wowhead’s Forever database.

data.objectivesText: Collect 8 Lady's Tear Moss.
description: If we are to save my fellows in the Nightclaw Den, I am going to need some ingredients for a poultice. The first and most important is a spindly moss called Lady's Tear. It typically grows on the base of the trees here in Shadowgale.
This moss secretes a sticky substance that acts as an antiseptic and is perfect for binding open wounds. I have gathered what little I can reach but I know there is more in this forest.
Go and be swift. We are going to need a lot if the injured I left behind still live.
data.partialDialogue: Have you found the Lady's Tear?
data.turnInDialogue: <Elegael takes the sticky mound of moss from you with a weak smile.>Thank you, Trogdorp, you have done well. This is exactly what we need.

data.objectivesText: Collect 20 feathers from the Shadowgale Shrieklings in Shadowgale Forest.
description: The other ingredient I need for the poultice is feathers from the Shadowgale shrieklings that roam this forest. In their juvenile form, the shrieklings have insulative feathers which would be ideal to put over the moss. These feathers will prevent the antiseptic sap from drying out and will provide at least some protection against the elements.
Be warned, the shrieklings are normally docile but they have been incredibly hostile of late. Their large talons can easily disembowel you if you aren't careful.
data.partialDialogue: It deeply saddens me to ask you to kill the young shrieklings, but with the rise in their aggression it is for the best. We can only handle so many emergencies at a time.
data.turnInDialogue: Thank you for these. I will be sure to use every feather so their sacrifice will not be in vain.

data.objectivesText: Collect 10 Bloodied Heirlooms from Al'Aketh Footsoldiers and Al'Aketh Stormchasers in the Shadowgale Forest.
description: The Al'aketh Cultists ambushed us with no warning, though their motives remain a mystery to me. I knew these cultists had clouds in-between their ears, but I never imagined they would upset the delicate balance here on Zephras with such brutality. Go, slay as many as you can and take their heirlooms if they wear any.
<Elegael spits.>
These storm cursed cultists don't deserve to be called shen'dorei. The beasts of the forest can have their bodies. Their ashes don't deserve the winds.
data.partialDialogue: I will make the cult pay for every drop of druid blood they have spilled this day.
data.turnInDialogue: <Elegael looks down at the collection of bloodied heirlooms with distress.>So many young lives with so much potential now gone forever. Thank you for returning these, ‹class›.I will hold onto them for safe keeping until I am able to take them to the High Elder. There they can go back into the collection and await the next and perhaps more worthy generation to come of age.

data.objectivesText: Kill Commander Haalien and bring his head to Elegael Thornpaw in the Shadowgale Forest.
description: The reason for cultists presence here still baffles me, but I smell a familiar scent over the bloodshed.
One of our circle druids, Haalien, disappeared months back. It appears he's thrown his sorry hide in with the cultists.
Show him what happens when he spills the blood of his kin! Take his head and return it to me.
data.partialDialogue: Are our brethren's lives truly worth so little to you, Haalien?
data.turnInDialogue: <Elegael grimaces at the severed head, but nods curtly.>Thank you, Thaildras. No matter how much rage I have within me, it would have been difficult to strike down my own cousin.Do not mourn for him. His ignorance and malice has killed many innocents this day.

knownStatus.changeNote: New in Forever.  From Wowhead’s Forever database.

data.objectivesText: Enter the Nightfang Den and heal 7 druids and find Jorel Windsinger in Shadowgale Forest.
description: I have finished the poultices. Quickly, take them to the druids in the cave, north just across the clearing. I know my brethren are in much more dire condition than I. They are likely too injured to heal their own wounds. There are so few of us shen'dorei druids that every life is precious.
Before you go, I have a selfish request. My mate, Jorel Windsinger was in dire condition when I left. Please, see to his wounds if he still lives.
data.partialDialogue: ‹class›! You have returned. Were you able to reach my brothers and sisters? Did you find Jorel?
data.turnInDialogue: <Elegael's face pales as you relay the fate of Jorel and the condition of the rest of the druids.>No... no! This is far worse than I had--<Elegael chokes back a sob, and grits her teeth letting out a pained snarl.>They will pay. They will ALL pay. Anyone who allies with the Al'aketh will feel my wrath! This I swear.

data.objectivesText: Bring the Ripped Missive to Elegael Thornpaw in the Shadowgale Forest.
description: <Tucked behind one of Haalien's bracers is a note that's been slightly torn and bloodstained in your fight. It looks like it contains useful information for about the cultist motivations for the attack on the druid den. Elegael would be interested in this intel.>
data.turnInDialogue: They were here for the pylon? But to what end? We were not the original reason for their attack?<Elegael trails off shaking with rage as she reads.>They murdered my people because we were an inconvenience! I shall tear apart every cultist with my fangs! I will make sure none leave this place with their lives.Go, swiftly! If the orders truly originated in Valanaar, it means it is likely a traitor hiding there. Give the missive to Lotheluum in Valannar and tell him what has transpired.

data.lede: A level 12 quest for both factions, from level 8.

knownStatus.raw: New in Forever.  From Wowhead’s Forever database.
knownStatus.changeNote: New in Forever.  From Wowhead’s Forever database.

data.objectivesText: Give the missive to Lotheluum in Valannar and tell him what has transpired.
description: It would appear that there is a correspondent hiding somewhere in Valanaar feeding information to the cult. I am clearly in no shape to make the journey, but Lotheluum needs to know what transpired here.
He should also know the fate of those who are no longer with us. Thanks to your help I think we can handle the rest of the situation from here, thought the damage has been done.
Please go swiftly, ‹name›. I hope our paths will cross again someday. Until then, I have cultists to slay.
data.turnInDialogue: <Lotheluum wears a look of genuine terror as you recount the events from the ‹class› den.>I--I'm sorry, Solarus. I need just a moment. There are no words I possess that can describe the loss.This is grave news indeed. If this missive is not fabricated, then we indeed have at best an accomplice and at worst a traitor here in Valanaar. I will take this to the High Elder immediately! I will not let my fellows sacrifice be in vain.

data.objectivesText: Speak with Elegael Thornpaw in the northeastern part of Shadowgale Forest.
description: Thank goodness our message got to Lotheluum. Wait, where are the rest of the reinforcements? Surely it is not just you they sent?
<Elegael pales as you explain yourself.>
So the message did not get to Valanaar. We are in dire straights indeed then.
<Elegael sighs deeply then looks resolute.>
Then we must handle this on our own. Time is of the essence.
data.turnInDialogue: The Al'aketh Cultists ambushed us with little to no warning. Many inside my den lay wounded or dying. I had attempted to send a message to Valanaar but it appears my efforts were in vain.Please, if you have come here I beg for your help. I don't know how much longer my fellows will be able to survive this onslaught.

data.objectivesText: Find Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan.
description: Long has it been since ye were last tested, ‹name›. Ye have shown patience thus far in yer studies, but the time has come for ye to learn about the purity of water.
Seek out Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan. He is along the north western edge o' the lake, south of Stonewrought Dam. Ye  will find him there at his burrow hut. Good luck to ye, ‹name›.
data.turnInDialogue: The wind's rushin' at yer back, the stone's firm beneath yer boots, and the fire in yer belly's burnin' bright. Aye, it's time ye learned the truth o' water's purity. Yer path's been long, but it's yer spirit that'll carry ye further still. Now, go on, take that first step. The mountain waits for no one.

data.objectivesText: Find Hervdana Saegrund in the Wetlands.
description: If there's one truth ye need to learn about water, it's this: water means rebirth. It carves stone, cleanses filth, and heals the weary -- but only when it's pure. Taint it, and it'll ruin all it touches.
If ye seek the water sapta, find Hervdana Saegrund in the Wetlands. Her family dwells in a cave beneath the southern falls.
Go on then, don't let the river outrun ye.
data.turnInDialogue: Aye, I see it in yer eyes, ‹race›. You're wonderin' what kind o' soul chooses to live out here, deep in the Wetlands, with Dark Iron scum lurkin' about and nary a guard in sight. Well, we all have our reasons, love.But the real question is, what brings you to our home? Out here at the edge of the falls, I reckon we both know the answer to that.

data.objectivesText: Fill the Empty Brown Waterskin at the bottom of the waterfalls below Hervdana's cave and return it to her in the Wetlands.
description: Ah, so ye've come seekin' the sapta, have ye? Well then, listen close, love. To find understandin' and earn the sapta, ye must seek water in its various forms. As ye gather the samples, keep yer eyes open. Watch the beasts that guard it, the land it nourishes, and how it changes lives.
We'll start simple: fill this skin at the base o' the falls, where the fresh meets the brackish. Go on now, and mind the marsh.
data.partialDialogue: I'm nearly ready to send ye off on the rest o' yer tasks. But tell me, have ye filled the skin yet? The ocean brings life, aye -- but it carries sediment, minerals, and energies far different from the snowmelt and springwater of the highlands. Where sea and spring meet, there's wisdom to be found.
data.turnInDialogue: Glad ye managed to steer clear o' the Dark Iron. Shame they've crept so far north--makes ye wonder what dwarfkind could do if the clans ever stopped squabblin' and worked as one.Still, the tides rise high when the moons are strong, and the seawater floods the marsh. It's here that we study our estuary water.Thank ye for this sacred offering, it marks the beginning of your stage as a vessel--one who seeks the waters' wisdom.

data.objectivesText: Fill the Empty Red Waterskin at Stonewatch Falls near the Nightcrawler Murlocs and return to Hervdana Saegrund in the Wetlands.
description: Aye, Redridge drinks deep from Lake Everstill, but by the time the waters tumble down Stonewatch Falls, somethin' has seeped in. The murlocs down there are big, twisted brutes. Not like the ones ye find here or in the Loch. Lucky for the townsfolk they keep to the base o' the falls.
Bring a sampling to me. I've a mind to find out if it's magic, venom, or somethin' worse that's taintin' the waters near that old fort.
data.partialDialogue: The folk o' Lakeshire don't ken how good they've got it -- fresh water flowin' right at their boots, keepin' their nets full, their crops green, and their coin purses jinglin'. Even when the kingdom's guard can barely spare a lad with a sword, they've got Everstill watchin' over 'em.
data.turnInDialogue: Aye, this is good water, Theinn. The magic used by the shadowseers in the region must be changin' the murlocs. Nothin' but pure water, this be. Yer dedication to the task at hand and abilities to seek out that which is needed proves you're ready for the next stage of your journey.One more sample is all I need to create the reagent needed for your sapta. Norric will be pleased as well.

data.objectivesText: Fill the Unfilled Blue Waterskin at the waters of Astranaar in Ashenvale and return to Hervdana Saegrund in the Wetlands.
description: Take this waterskin and journey deep into the emerald shade o' Ashenvale. Astranaar rests cradled by waters untouched by corruption. Ruins litter the bed o' the lake, hinting at a bygone era. Bring back a sample from the lake. Pure, ancient, and possibly enchanted water.
It's the last liquid I need before I send ye back to Norric.
Board the boat in Menethil to Auberdine, it stops in Southshore on the way over.
And mind yerself... the forest's got eyes, and they don't blink.
data.partialDialogue: Do you have the water yet, Theinn? If ye haven't made the trek to Kalimdor yet, be careful.
data.turnInDialogue: Well done, Theinn! With all three samples in hand, I'll brew ye a vial o' water so pure it'd make the mountains weep. It's the final piece for yer rite o' passage. I'm proud to call ye kin, Theinn. Ye've done ‹class› proud, and I look forward to hearing yer tales in the future.

data.objectivesText:
Cleanse the corruption at Stendel's Pond in Westfall.
Return to Norric in Loch Modan when finished.
description: In Westfall, outside o' Moonbrook lies Stendel's Pond. Once a pure spring, now touched by dark forces. The spirits there 'ave gone silent.

Ye must face the corruption that fouls the waters. Take its bracers and the last drops o' Hervdana's potion, then place 'em on the shrine. That'll call forth a spirit, cleansed and true. Speak with it, learn what ye can.
Bring me proof the deed's done, and I'll grant ye the totem.
data.partialDialogue: The shrine stands aged and forgotten, cloaked in dust and cobwebs. The pond beside it lies eerily still, its surface untouched by wind or life. Scattered along the shore are the bones of beasts once burdened by labor. The water's murky sheen raises a troubling question--has it been poisoned by the surrounding malaise, or is it the very source of it?
data.turnInDialogue: You place the bracers atop the shrine and then pour the remaining drops of Norric's potion into dry stone. You begin to incant the simple words Norric taught you and the droplets vaporize atop the stone within the bindings....

data.objectivesText: Find and kill Ur'endra in the Shen'dar Highlands.
description: You have come to me in hopes of learning to take a shape of strength. I have a task for you, though it lays heavy on my heart.

My mate, Ur'endra, has lost herself to madness and has begun to attack her own kin. Without the winds many creatures have begun to lose themselves, and with Ur'endra's great might she poses a dire threat to the delicate balance. She roams the Shen'dar Highlands to the northwest of here.
Show me you have the fortitude to end her suffering and I shall grant you my blessing.
data.turnInDialogue: The agony I feel over her loss is immeasurable, but it is what is necessary for the balance. You have demonstrated a resolve to persevere, even when a terrible price is asked.You have done well, ‹class›. I shall grant you the blessing to take on the shape of my kin. Be a beacon for those that lack the strength to persevere and a defender of those in need.Go now, and embrace the way of the claw, child.

data.objectivesText: Collect 8 Abandoned Belongings from the ruins of Ban'aethal.
description: You look like a capable adventurer. Do you happen to be headed towards Shadowgale Forest? Ban'aethal lies deep in the forest; that's where we're all from.
<Ealaane gestures to the other refugees.>

We've recently had to evacuate Ban'aethal, as it began to fall into the sky. It was sudden and in the middle of the night. If you are headed that way, would you please look for any belongings left behind? The forest and village are far too dangerous for us to return to now.
data.partialDialogue: So many of us left with nothing more than the clothes on our backs. Any belongings you might recover would be cherished.
data.turnInDialogue: Thank you, ‹class›, you have done a great kindness to us refugees this day. I will make sure to return these to their owners. At least it gives us a place to start over from.

data.objectivesText: Find Resaan in the Ruins of Ban'aethal.
description: If you are traveling to Ban'aethal, I have a selfish request. My love, Resaan... I believe is no longer a part of this world. He had tried to go back to get supplies even though I begged him to stay. It has been over a week already and I fear the worst.
Please, if you find him bring him home. If he has perished then I beg you to please bring me his heirloom.
data.partialDialogue: Have you any news of Resaan? Please, ‹class›, the wait is hard to endure after everything that has happened.
data.turnInDialogue: <Ealaane's eyes well with tears.>Oh, Resaan my love. What will become of us now? There was so much... it feels as if our lives together had just started.Thank you, ‹class›. The world is cruel to take both my home and my love from me. At least his heirloom will give me some closure.

description: Greetings, young ‹race›. I can see that you have much promise in the druidic arts. There is one who you may want to speak with in the city of Thunder Bluff by the name of Turak Runetotem. He will teach you how to reach the stronghold of the Cenarion Circle on Kalimdor, Moonglade.
You will be welcomed there, and the druids of the circle will impart their knowledge upon you.
As your people would say--go with the wind's blessing, young one. I wish you good fortune in your adventures.
data.turnInDialogue: A high elf, speaking to me... in Thunder Bluff. Will wonders never cease?Well, shaper of wind, let me join our Earthen Ring brothers and sisters in welcoming you to Azeroth. My fellow druids of the Cenarion Circle have much wisdom to impart upon you, child of nature.

description: Greetings, young ‹class›.

Have you heard of the Cenarion Circle? I'd expect not. They are an ancient order of naturalists and practitioners of the druidic arts, much like yourself. In the city of Stormwind you'll find a night elf by the name of Sheldras Moontree. He will teach you how to reach the stronghold of the Cenarion Circle on Kalimdor, a place called Moonglade.
Go now. You have much to learn if you wish to save your home.
data.turnInDialogue: Greetings, fellow ‹class›. It pleases me to meet a fellow ‹class› from among the Skyborne, and to be among the first to welcome you to Azeroth.I think you will find that my fellow druids of the Cenarion Circle have much wisdom to impart upon you, child of nature.

Fret not though, one of our mages will be waiting to receive you upon your arrival in Dalaran. I'd encourage you to explore Azeroth while we set our affairs in order here. We will call upon you when you are needed.

description: Its a big world down here, and we need our people to start branching out to explore it. That's where you come in.

The Kirin Tor is a member of an "Alliance" of like-minded nations. The de-facto heart of this alliance is the city of Stormwind to the south. Elaadrin has asked me to find someone to travel to Stormwind and meet with the regent lord there, a human named Bolvar Fordragon.
When you are ready, the Kirin Tor mages have set up a special portal for the High Order to use to access Stormwind.
data.turnInDialogue: Well met, ‹class›. I am Bolvar Fordragon, regent to the throne of Stormwind.A Kirin Tor messenger told me to expect an emissary from the High Order, and here you stand. It's been some time since a high elf has stood in this throne room, but I am glad to accept you now as a guest.On behalf of the King, I welcome you to Stormwind and give you leave to travel freely through alliance lands. Welcome to Azeroth, Skyborne.

data.objectivesText: Speak with Lumina Windsinger in the Sepulcher.
description: I think you should know that it wasn't actually the Gnolls who attacked us on the road.

We were actually attacked by a giant, wolf-like creature that I now know as a "worgen". It dispatched our guards and came for me, but Banon threw himself in its path. I managed to get a spell off which startled the creature, causing it to flee, but Banon was already badly bitten. He insisted I leave him there but I refused.
We were limping back here when the gnolls found us. What came next was terrifying...
data.turnInDialogue: So now you understand. At the very end of his strength after being pierced by a dozen gnoll blades, he reared up to strike me. In that final moment we locked eyes, and I could tell he still knew who he was and that he recognized me. He knew what was happening but he had no control over himself. That was the worst part.If such a thing is possible, I will see the creature that doomed him dead so that it can never visit this horror on another living thing. I swear it upon the sky above.

That's the one that attacked us. He is known as Old Fire-Eye and he is the biggest and meanest of their kind. To put him down, we'll need a special kind of weapon.

description: Before we fled Gnomeregan, I made a hard copy of my family's archives. Arcanotechnical field equations, Second War submarine hull designs, Grandma Quikswitch's chili recipe... our greatest accomplishments are in those files.
It wasn't until we reached Ironforge that I found a hole in my pack! Several punch cards are gone, and without them the data's too scrambled to recover.
The cards must be buried in the snow, somewhere outside Gnomeregan. Could you find them? I know it's a long shot...
data.partialDialogue: How is the data retrieval progressing?
data.turnInDialogue: These cards seem a bit damp... but I can work with this! Thank you, Archnatum!

data.objectivesText: Bring a Kor Gem to Ulric Frostveil in Ashenvale.
description: A Forsaken paladin... here in Ashenvale? Amusing.
So you seek a Kor Gem? Unsurprising as these are sometimes employed to empower magical weapons and implements by the paladins of the alliance. Why should a fallen paladin like you be any different?
If you truly desire one of the gems, then you must head north to the ruins known as Blackfathom Deeps. The naga who still use the gems are down below. Do not go alone, ‹class›.
data.partialDialogue: Kor gems can be used for great acts of evil. Far be it from me to judge if your intentions are pure. It matters not to me.
data.turnInDialogue: You'll no doubt notice the corruption that permeates this gem. For your purposes, The magic needed to dispel the evil that the naga witches have infused into the gem is rather simple. A shame really, there's much one could learn from such powers.I don't suppose you'd be willing to abandon whatever quest caused you seek this gem, and sell it to me instead? It could prove valuable to my... academic pursuits.

description: What a view... Best an old man can ask for.

The fish sure are bitin' now, though I'm down to my last bait. I don't suppose you have any spare fishing supplies on you? Of course not, forgive me. I get so excited at the thought of casting another line it didn't dawn on me I may be one of the few carrying supplies everywhere I go.
Would you be able to help refresh my stock? Catherine Leland has an assortment of fishing goods just west of the Trade District along the canals. Tell her old Gray sent you.
data.partialDialogue: Did you get the fishing supplies?
data.turnInDialogue: Great timing! Caught a big one with my last bait. Great day so far. They're really biting out here!Tell you what, since you were kind enough to keep this old man in business how about a few fish for the road?

data.objectivesText: Speak with Ott and ask him to forge your blade.
description: In Tarren Mill there is a weaponsmith known as Ott. By all accounts he is an unremarkable smith, selling simple blades to travelers. I purchased a sword from him myself, and when I took it to the undercity for maintenance some time later, the smiths there were surprised at its quality. They assumed it came from a well known master smith, but no, it was just Ott.
I'd like to give this orc a chance to do something truly special. Take the materials to Ott in Tarren Mill and offer him the commission.
data.partialDialogue: Are you in need of a blade, ‹class›?
data.turnInDialogue: Interesting. I don't think anyone has ever asked me to actually carry out a custom commission for them. Mostly I just make humble, functional weapons in my own style. It's not much, but its honest work and I don't seek accolades or glory.I'm happy to try, but why would you seek me for this? There are plenty of smiths in the Undercity that will take on custom jobs like this.

data.partialDialogue: Is it done? Is the beast slain?

description: If you're looking for Jeremy Heartweaver, your best bet is to talk to his newly adopted mother, Avette Fellwood out in Duskwood. Sweet woman. Likely needs another pair of hands for her work, but it beats staying in the orphanage.
If you see little Jeremy do be sure to tell him we're all thinking of him, won't you?
data.partialDialogue: Yes? What do you need?
data.turnInDialogue: Oh no...It's nice of you to bring this, but I don't think Jeremy is ready to see it. Matron Nightingale said my little Jeremy hasn't spoken since the attack on Lordaeron, and I don't intend to force him now. Showing him this will only cause him more pain.Don't look at me like that. I won't hide his past from him, but he needs time to heal. I'll give this to him when he's older. Thank you for stopping by, but I think it's time you should go.

description: What do you want, ‹race›? Can't you see there is a war to be won?
My master has already charged into the fray and has ordered me to maintain my post. It has been quite some time, however.

I doubt you'll survive ten minutes in combat, but if it keeps your simple mind busy, why don't you seek out the Grand Marshal. He is the tallest, most statuesque hero you've ever laid eyes on. You'll know him when you see him.

data.objectivesText: Collect 8 Bottles of Whispering Elixir from Shadowvale, then return to Carolai Anise in Brill.
description: Before the Scourge invasion, the reclusive village of Shadowvale was known for its Whispering Elixir. Distilled from herbs found only in Tyr's Fall, the elixir was sought by apothecaries, mystics, and poisoners alike even after being banned in the city.

I've had requests from a number of buyers eager to get their hands on some elixir. Travel to the ruins of Shadowvale deep in the Whispering Forest to the west. I'm prepared to offer significant compensation if you can recover some bottles for me.
data.partialDialogue: I trust you did not get lost?
data.turnInDialogue: You say there is evil in Shadowvale? I admit, I am not surprised. The forest folk were an odd lot, and they did not care for visitors. Some believe the Whispering Forest itself is cursed, and the elixir distilled from its roots carries that same curse......but enough of superstition and rumors, He. Thank you for the elixirs. Here, take this as payment.

data.objectivesText: Take the skycutter ship from Zephras Isle to Mulgore and speak with Alana Stormwalker when you arrive.
description: The recent events with the cult have delayed my plans to travel to Azeroth and I must remain here in Valanaar for a time. You and a handful of other Windshapers will be our vanguard instead. Alaana Stormwalker will be waiting to receive you upon your arrival in Mulgore, and I'd encourage you to explore Azeroth while we finish our business here. We will join you soon.
When you are ready, please proceed to the dock just outside this lodge and board the skycutter ship there. Banu-Alah, ‹name›.
data.turnInDialogue: More adventurers from Zephras, I see. Wonderful. The winds surely favor us! It's going to take us some time to get ourselves established here, so you may want to take some time to explore this new land.Azeroth is an exciting new world, but it's also a dangerous world. You'd do well to prepare yourself for this new adventure by familiarizing yourself with the lands nearby.

data.objectivesText: Travel to Orgrimmar and speak with Thrall in the Valley of Wisdom.
description: Its a big world down here, and our new allies are the key to our survival.
The Earthen Ring is a member of the "Horde", a proud collection of like-minded peoples. The nearby city of Thunder Bluff is a part of the horde, and further to the east lies the capital of Orgrimmar.

Seek out the flight master in the center of Thunder Bluff. They will fly you to Orgrimmar where you will make contact with the horde warchief--Thrall, on behalf of the Windshapers. Winds guide you, ‹name›.
data.turnInDialogue: Lok-tar, ‹class›. I am Thrall, Warchief of the Horde.An Earthen Ring messenger told me to expect an emissary from the Windshapers, and here you are. I'd not have expected to see a high elf standing before me here in Orgrimmar, but the horde will welcome you as our guest all the same.You have my blessing to travel through horde lands. Go with honor, Windshaper.

description: I need someone with a strong sword arm and some extra time on their hands to help me gather some lion hides. It stings my pride to ask a stranger for this aid, but I took an injury to my leg recently. Until I heal, I'm in no shape to go hunting myself but I have obligations to keep.
The big ones in this area generally have the best hides, so start with those first.
data.partialDialogue: How goes the hunt?
data.turnInDialogue: Yes, these look like they will do nicely. I have an arrangement with a local tanner to deliver these raw hides in exchange for various finished leather goods that I use as part of my trade.I've never come up short on my end of the arrangement, and even with my injury I do not intend to start now.

description: Yes, I used to be a member of the Kul Tiras navy. After Lord Admiral took Theramore and started his campaign in Durotar, I had... "objections" to his methods. Particularly the methods involving executing civilians.
There's more to the story but... wait... what's that?
There's a group of men coming up the ridge!

description: The healer who saved me could not save her, and she has died in battle. Her name is Olgra, and I will never forget her.
You did not find her adornments on her body? She wore many jewels of polished bone.
Slay the Razormane Raiders near where she fell, and find her precious works of art!
I will place them with the memorial that I build in her memory.
data.partialDialogue: I have only memories now, but I will build a tribute to Olgra so that they never fade.

description: Now that we've claimed the head of the tarnished commander, I need you to deliver it to the Undercity. Sylvanas Windrunner mistrusts us greatly, and all but openly disparages us.
Deliver Rudolph Gelhardt's head to the Dark Lady. Show her that we tend to our own house and are devoted to the prosperity of the forsaken.
data.partialDialogue: Why are you addressing me, ‹class›?
data.turnInDialogue: I don't doubt Danitha's sincerity and desire to earn a place for your kind amongst the Forsaken. However, I suspect that this isn't the last time we'll see one of your brothers and sisters go mad and turn the light against their own people.There may come a time when I decide that tolerating your misbegotten order is no longer in the best interests of the Forsaken. I suggest you continue to serve your people diligently.We will be watching.

description: The sun and the moon, An'she and Mu'sha, are not part of our world like the elements, yet their light gives us life, guidance, and hope.
We pay respect to the spirits of the world, and so we pay respect to the twins as well.

If you would show your respect, take this smoldering incense and bring it to a shrine in the hills to the southeast, overlooking the mesa, south of the quilboar. Be quick, so that you can reach the shrine before the incense burns away.
Don't get it wet!

description: Taking away their pendants is just the first step. If the Kirin Tor really are shipping a steady supply of relics from Dalaran, we must stop them at the source.

Search the roads around Ambermill for Dalaran's wizards and watchers. Their presence has allowed free access across our borders for too long. If we can cull their numbers, that should put a stop to these pendants making it into Silverpine Forest in the first place.
data.turnInDialogue: Ever since the barrier went down around Dalaran, the Kirin Tor have maintained a death grip on the roads. They're paranoid about something, that much is certain.For now, however, the why is irrelevant.

data.turnInDialogue: These Dark Irons may be our cousins but they ain't family, that's for sure. I shed no tears for any misfortune that befalls them that stray too far from that accursed mountain o' theirs.Hopefully this is enough to put 'em off of further incursions into these lands.

data.objectivesText: Deliver the Dark Iron Map to Earthseer Farsen in Dun Morogh.
description: <The map you are holding seems to show a complex series of underground tunnels and highways that all seem to converge on a point underneath Ironforge itself.

You can't be sure what the runes say as they are written in the ugly jagged rune language of the Dark Iron dwarves, but you can guess at the purpose of these tunnels. As you are reading the map, a gust of wind washes over you and you can faintly hear a dwarven voice carried on it. Earthseer Farsen needs to see this.>
data.partialDialogue: Oh what's this, then?
data.turnInDialogue: Juding by this map, it certainly looks like these Dark Irons are planning some sort of incursion into the vaults beneath Ironforge. The band ye busted up to the east must be a scouting force.Thank ye for bringing me this. If we hurry, we might be able to beat them to whatever their goal is down there.

data.objectivesText: Enter the Hall of Thanes beneath Old Ironforge and claim the Head of Durgen Dirgehammer.
description: Gather some allies and head down into the caverns beneath Old Ironforge. Enter the Hall of Thanes there and push to the lower vaults.
My Dark Iron is a bit rusty, but I can make out a name--one Durgen Dirgehammer. It's likely that he's the commander. Take his head and deliver it to King Magni Bronzebeard.
Oh, and when you do, tell him his old friend Farsen sends his regards!
data.partialDialogue: What do ye need, citizen?
data.turnInDialogue: A Dark Iron incursion--right beneath our feet? Well, I'm relieved to hear that the Dark Iron commander has been dispatched.The guards will head in and clean up the rest of the rabble. We'll see to it that the breaches are sealed and the lower levels reinforced to ensure that no further incursions are possible.Thank ye for yer service to Ironforge,‹class›. Take this as a small token of my gratitude. Oh, and if ye see that old Wildhammer rockhugger Farsen again, tell 'em to pay me a proper visit.

data.objectivesText: Collect 8 Dwarven Heirlooms from the Hall of Thanes.
description: You there, adventurer... I could really use your aid.

I was sneaking--uh... 'patrolling' in the vaults when a force of Dark Iron dwarves emerged from the depths in mole machines! I don't know what they are here for, but there is priceless loot--uh or, rather... I mean, 'important cultural heirlooms' down there! Please, recover any such relics you see and return them here.
I assure you that anything you recover will be catalogued and returned to its proper place of honor.
data.partialDialogue: <Thom appears to absentmindedly rub his hands together as he looks at you.>
data.turnInDialogue: Look at you, as brave as you are enterprising! I'm a gnome of my word, and your reward is well earned!Now, let me take a look at the haul--uh, I mean... the recovered heirlooms. I need to get started appraising--excuse me, 'cataloging' them so that they can be put back in their proper places as quickly as possible.

data.objectivesText: Sit near Brakk's Basic Campfire by typing /sit in the chat window and wait until you receive the Boosted Rest buff.
description: Greetings, ‹class›. I can see you've got the look of an adventurer about you. This is good. The world needs more of us restless souls, seeking fortune and glory.
You'll need to learn to thrive in the wilds to be successful in this line of work. Not sure how your outdoor skills are but I can probably teach you a thing or two, if you'd be apt to learn.
Have a seat near the fire and get comfortable. I'll walk you through it.
data.partialDialogue: Having the skills needed to survive the outdoors are critical. A well-rested and well-prepared adventurer has a much higher chance of surviving this lifestyle.
data.turnInDialogue: So now that we've learned the basics, why don't you go and learn a tradeskill from the trainers in the village nearby. They will also teach you how to create a camp fixture suitable to your new profession.

data.objectivesText: Cook Torka in Razor Hill wants you to collect 8 Prickly Pear Fruit from the Razormane Grounds west of town.
description: Our hunters and fishers bring back plenty of savory food for our troops - but it's rare that they get a sweet treat.

I've seen a cactus that produces a prickly, tasty fruit. But it only grows in the hills to the west, where the wretched quilboars make their camps. Make your way past the quilboars and bring me some of those fruits. And be careful - the fruits are as spiny as the quilboars!
data.partialDialogue: Did you find the fruits?
data.turnInDialogue: I'll use these to prepare something tasty, and save the seeds for planting. Someday we'll have prickly pears growing all around Orgrimmar!

data.objectivesText: Pa'zula in Sen'jin Village wants you to collect 3 Luminous Residue. Luminous Residue can be obtained by disenchanting Hexed Pendants dropped by trolls in the Echo Isles.
description: The trolls east of here have lost their will to the witchdoctor, Zalazane. He uses many cruel magics to keep hold of his prisoners' minds, but one of his favorite tricks is to make them wear pendants wrapped in evil binding spells.
Practice your enchanting skills by stripping the magic from these pendants, and bring me the results. And don't accidentally put one around your neck, if you value your freedom!
data.partialDialogue: What do you have for me, Thay?
data.turnInDialogue: Fine work. A shame about the slain trolls, but with the binding spells removed, their spirits can rest.

data.objectivesText: Find the Argent Dawn member near the entrance to the Undercity.
description: Not sure if you heard, but two emissaries of the Argent Dawn just passed through here. I don't mind the Argent Dawn, but I don't like them poking around Tirisfal unsupervised either. They were both Forsaken... but that doesn't make me any less nervous.

One of them just passed by here, headed southeast. There's a group of scourge cultists snooping around the outskirts of the city in that direction. If those two heard about them, there's no doubt that would have caught their attention.
data.turnInDialogue: Stay low and try not to be seen, ‹class›. These cultists are not to be trifled with.

data.objectivesText: Observe the conversation between Danitha Morr and Leonid Barthalomew the Revered.
description: Danitha and I fought against the scourge in the defense of the Undercity when Naxxramas attacked. We lost many good friends that day, including the hero after which this keep was named--Garek Bandarion.
He might just have been the first Forsaken to rediscover how to wield the light as a paladin. I am encouraged to see his legacy and potential live on here with Danitha and her cohort.
If only the rest of the forsaken felt the same way...
data.turnInDialogue: I plan to stay here for a time and speak with more of my friends, but I will return to Light's Hope Chapel in Eastern Plaguelands soon enough. Should you ever find yourself out that way, please do say hello. We could use always use more help from able-bodied adventurers.

data.objectivesText: Gather 12 Necrotic Crystal Fragments in Tirisfal Glades.
description: It wasn't long ago that the citadel of Naxxramas bore down upon this city, intent on wiping the Forsaken off the map. Both the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn lost much that day to secure the future of the Forsaken.

During the battle, the great necrotic focusing crystal hanging beneath Naxxramas was shattered and its fragments were scattered all over this area. I suspect that is what the cultists are here for. Help me recover the fragments and deprive the scourge of them.
data.partialDialogue: I'd advise you not come into too much physical contact with those crystals. Even shattered and spent, the lingering magic in these necrotic crystals is highly dangerous.
data.turnInDialogue: Thank you. This should slow the efforts of the scourge in this area. I suspect the denizens of Tirisfal will be pulling these crystals out of the ground for years, but removing the most conspicuous of them can only help.

data.objectivesText: Meet Leonid Barthalomew at Bandarion Keep in Tirisfal Glades.
description: You've done a great thing for the cause of the Argent Dawn here today, and I thank you. I don't know how familiar you are with the fortress of Bandarion Keep, but my commander and I were headed that way to meet with the paladins that reside there. That was before we learned of the presence of the Cult of the Damned.
If you'd like to learn more about the Argent Dawn and our mission, seek out my commander at Bandarion Keep, to the northwest of here. I'll remain here to mop up the rest of this mess.
data.turnInDialogue: This place is full of memories for me. This place was once held by the Argent Dawn. It was here from here that we prepared for many battles and skirmishes against the scourge during their most recent push into Tirisfal Glades.When we withdrew to the Plaguelands I feared it would fall into disrepair. My fear was well-founded, but I am glad that Danitha and her paladins have taken over stewardship of it now.She even named the keep after... a mutual friend.
